messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: control-plane 5xx rate > 8% over 3m for /v1/auth/validate and /v1/org/lookup. Routing errors + timeouts. Auto-pager to @jamie_oncall and @kelly_sre :rotating_light:
jamie_oncall: on it. I'm pulling traces now. Any customer-facing alerts?
maria_pm: Support reporting elevated 502s for API keys validation — several customers on Dedicated seeing errors. ETA on root cause?
sanjay_eng: quick glance of traces: auth service calls to billing and org-lookup show long tails; a lot of upstream 504s from org-lookup cache tier. Could be a cache eviction storm.
kelly_sre: noted. Starting runbook: isolate auth traffic, enable fallback cache, and scale org-lookup pool. Tagging runbook steps.
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP 1: increase deployment org-lookup replicas by +3: kubectl scale deploy/org-lookup --replicas=6 -n controlplane.
jamie_oncall: doing the scale now.
jamie_oncall: kubectl exec -n controlplane deployctl -- curl -s http://org-lookup.monitor/health => several 500s and high p95 latency 2.1s.
sanjay_eng: can we temporarily open the circuit-breaker to avoid auth syncing with billing for non-critical paths? That would reduce symptom load.
kelly_sre: agree. Plan: 1) scale org-lookup 2) flip auth -> org-lookup fallback to cached responses (ttl-stale) 3) open billing circuit for non-blocking flows. I'll coordinate.
maria_pm: notify customers after mitigation starts. We should mark production degraded.
jamie_oncall: applied replica scale, new pods coming up (4/6 ready).
jamie_oncall: applying cached-fallback feature flag to auth: POST /flags/auth/fallback {"enabled": true} => response 200.
sanjay_eng: enabling billing circuit for non-critical endpoints: PATCH /config/circuits/billing?paths=token-introspect&mode=open => applied.
incident-bot: Update: 5xx rate decreased to 3.6% over 2m after scale + fallbacks.
kelly_sre: good signal. I still see occasional 502s from a subset of org-lookup shards. Investigating pod logs for OOMs or startup errors.
jamie_oncall: logs show repeated error: "org-lookup: redis cluster timeout: MOVED or ASK response" on shard-3. Could be coordinator misrouting after recent config rollout.
sanjay_eng: rollback config rollout that touched redis routing happened ~1766998500. I'll check the config server.
kelly_sre: in the meantime, I'll cordon and restart the problematic org-lookup pods to rejoin cluster.
jamie_oncall: cordon+restart done for org-lookup-3a. Pod restarted and joined cluster. Health checks pass.
incident-bot: metric: control-plane 5xx now 1.1% over last 1m. Latency p95 back to baseline for most routes.
maria_pm: good — sending interim note to customers: "We're investigating increased 5xx responses affecting auth/org-lookup; mitigations in progress. Some keys may see transient failures."
kelly_sre: prepping postmortem notes: root cause hypothesis = config rollout that misrouted redis shard traffic + cache stampede exposing org-lookup tail latency. Will collect logs and rollout diff.
sanjay_eng: I pulled config diff: a TTL-related optimization inadvertently changed slot mapping for one shard. Rolling that patch back now: PATCH /configs/controlplane/redis -> rollback to v12 => applied.
jamie_oncall: after rollback, consistent redis responses, no MOVED errors in logs.
incident-bot: final update: control-plane error rate stable <0.5% for 10m. Incident auto-resolve scheduled if stable for 30m.
maria_pm: creating support ticket batch & customer outreach templates. Assigning to @ops_support to send updates.
kelly_sre: post-incident actions: 1) add pre-rollout integration test for redis slot mapping 2) add throttled rollout for config-server changes 3) add alert tuning to catch cache eviction storms earlier.
jamie_oncall: handing off to @sanjay_eng for root-cause investigation and PMs for customer comms. I'll stay available for follow-up.
sanjay_eng: will own RCA and timeline. Uploading traces and logs to /incidents/1767000000/analysis.
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP COMPLETE: mitigation steps logged. Recommended follow-up checklist created.
incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (auto) in 30m if no new events."
